sentence: This project studies the causes of cancer, its risk and outcomes, from prevention to survivorship, and tests ways to reduce gaps in cancer care.
This project builds computational methods that use RNA-sequencing data to find which genes are active in human cells.
This project studies how radiation, then an injection of dendritic cells into the tumor, plus standard inhibitors, affects patients with hepatocellular carcinoma.
This project studies how support cells in the brain control the firing of neurons and how they change brain function in disease and injury.
This project builds big data methods to study the genetic, molecular and neurobiological mechanisms of Alzheimer's disease and to find drugs for repurposing.
This project tries to find out how cellular environments change the behavior of biomolecules and so affect biological function and disease.
This project builds antibody drugs that protect against Marburg virus and tests a cocktail of them in animals.
This project works to make cancer detection by imaging more accurate and consistent across many imaging systems and sites, using artificial intelligence.
This project studies how a genetic cause of severe congenital neutropenia stops the body making mature, functional neutrophils.
This project studies how mixtures of air pollutants and heat affect placental insufficiency during pregnancy, using machine learning.
This project builds a rapid, non-invasive test that uses CRISPR to detect nontuberculous mycobacteria infections, find drug resistance and track treatment response.
This project studies the role of genetics, epigenetics and endocrinology in cardiometabolic diseases.
This project tries to find out how human tumor viruses cause Burkitt Lymphoma and Primary Effusion Lymphomas.
This project studies the genetic architecture of Alzheimer's Disease and related dementias, including age-related changes, using biobanks, electronic medical records and machine learning.
This project builds automated methods to check the quality of MRI data on cerebral blood flow and make it consistent across many sites.
This project studies how the 3D shape of tissue, such as curvature, affects the form, gene expression and behavior of cells in skin.
This project studies how stress at many levels affects tobacco use over time among young adults with and without access to tobacco cessation programs.
This project tries to find out how a cholesterol receptor in adipocytes controls lipid buildup in adipose tissue caused by a high-fat diet.
This project tests a vaccine strategy against Kaposi sarcoma-associated herpesvirus in nonhuman primates.
This project builds self-amplifying RNA in lipid nanoparticles for solid tumors and tests how many genes it can carry and express.
